extracted.intended_audience: writers and readers of humorous caricature; humorists and cultural commentators interested in English national personification
extracted.subtask_description: Sketching a national personification in humorous prose by assembling recurring traits, domestic detail, and comic habits (exemplified by the figure of John Bull). Useful for humorists creating broad, recognisable caricatures of a people or nation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of caricature and ludicrous nicknames
rubrics_metrics.description: Caricaturing and giving ludicrous appellations or nicknames (e.g., John Bull) is a prime species of English humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personify nations or groups with a single comic figure or name to capture and satirize national oddities; keep the epithet memorable and broadly descriptive rather than subtle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer blunt, comic, familiar personification to heroic idealization
rubrics_metrics.description: In personifying a nation, choose a blunt, comic, and familiar figure rather than something grand or heroic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the caricature accessible and domestic (e.g., 'a sturdy, corpulent old fellow with a three-cornered hat') — the comic power comes from homely, exaggerated detail rather than lofty traits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetition cements the caricature
rubrics_metrics.description: Continual contemplation and repeated portraits fix the caricature upon the national mind, and the nation may adapt to its own caricature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use recurring motifs and repeated jokes so the persona becomes recognizable and self-reinforcing; beware that repetition can shape real behavior and justify faults as traits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize plainness and matter-of-fact character
rubrics_metrics.description: John Bull is 'a plain, downright, matter-of-fact fellow, with much less of poetry about him than rich prose.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray the figure as practical and prosaic; concretize with everyday actions and down-to-earth language rather than romantic or idealized description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor broad humor over subtle wit
rubrics_metrics.description: He 'excels in humor more than in wit; is jolly rather than gay.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for hearty, broadly accessible comic effects (laughs, crude jokes, comic situations) rather than refined epigrams; the persona should provoke laughter more than admiration for cleverness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray emotional range: ready to laugh or cry, but loathes sentimentality
rubrics_metrics.description: Can be 'surprised into a broad laugh' or 'easily moved to a sudden tear' yet 'loathes sentiment and has no turn for light pleasantry.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show sudden, strong emotional reactions without indulging in delicate or effete sentimentality; emphasize caricatured affect rather than nuanced feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make him a boon companion and local champion
rubrics_metrics.description: A boon companion who will 'stand by a friend in a quarrel with life and purse.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depict loyalty and a readiness to defend neighbors as part of the comic virtue — he is generous in social allegiance even if flawed in other ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a fondness for contention (likes the beginning of fights)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fond of being in the midst of contention; 'only relishes the beginning of an affray' and 'always goes into a fight with alacrity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create scenes where the persona eagerly joins disputes but is poor at aftermaths — this asymmetry (eager starter, poor finisher) is a recurring comic trait.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrasting extravagance and scrimping economy
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternates between ostentatious public extravagance (treating neighbors, betting) and private parsimony: extravagant one day, miserly the next.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use oscillation between lavish public displays and petty private stinginess as a humorous behavioral pattern; show the rationale (economy aimed to enable the next spree).

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy as mechanism to enable extravagance
rubrics_metrics.description: His economy is 'of a whimsical kind, its chief object being to devise how he may afford to be extravagant.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray thrift not as principled frugality but as tactical saving for theatrical generosity — a comic motive that explains inconsistent behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make domestic hospitality prominent
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'bountiful provider and a hospitable housekeeper' whose household is enormously expensive in consumption and retainers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail the large, comfortable domestic establishment (food, servants, animals) to signal social status and the persona's contradictory virtues: generous at home despite petty habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctual payment combined with grumbling
rubrics_metrics.description: He is 'the most punctual and discontented paymaster in the world, drawing his coin out of his breeches pocket with infinite reluctance.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray fiscal reliability combined with vocal dissatisfaction as a comic trait: pays fully but complains at every transaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proneness to be gulled and justified generosity
rubrics_metrics.description: Prone to be gulled by strangers and to pay extravagantly for absurdities, excusing it as 'munificence.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use gullibility and self-justifying explanations (munificence) to create ironic situations where the caricature's virtues are also his weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defend coarse tastes as plainness
rubrics_metrics.description: Coarseness of taste and insensibility to foreign refinements are excused as being a 'plain John Bull.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame cultural parochialism as a proud plainness; let the persona dismiss refinement as affectation to comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argue faults into merits
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the name of John Bull he will 'argue every fault into a merit' — using the persona as a rhetorical defense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how the caricature rationalizes shortcomings; this self-justifying rhetoric is itself a source of humor and social critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meddlesome tendency in local affairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuously 'volunteering his services to settle his neighbor’s affairs' but often producing quarrels and being railingly ungracious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depict well-intentioned interference that ends in comic messes; this active meddling supplies situational comedy and exposes social foibles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physicality and mastery of local defensive arts
rubrics_metrics.description: Has learned 'the noble science of defence' (boxing and cudgel-play) and is quick to show physical readiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include physical bravado and readiness for combat as markers of the persona's masculinity and comic vanity; physical detail (cudgel, boxing) grounds scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend petty rights into exaggerated dignity
rubrics_metrics.description: Has 'filaments' of pride and policy stretching everywhere so that 'no event can take place without infringing some of his finely-spun rights and dignities.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exaggerate minor sensibilities into grand claims of honor to produce comic overreaction; show how trivial matters become matters of dignity for the persona.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use architectural and domestic detail to connote tradition
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the family mansion (old castellated manor-house, accumulations of parts and ages) to signal rootedness and venerability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ concrete architectural descriptions to suggest history and social standing; juxtapose venerable setting with comic personal traits to heighten irony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caricature can be used to excuse prejudice
rubrics_metrics.description: The caricature 'has gradually adapted itself to the nation' and 'they sometimes make their boasted Bullism an apology for their prejudice or grossness.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge the ethical risk: humorous personae may be misused to rationalize bigotry or coarse behavior. Effective satire should be aware of and, where appropriate, critique that danger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use local color and idiom to fix authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: References to 'homebred', 'sound of Bow bells', and local pastimes ground the persona in place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include regional idioms, institutions, and pastimes to make the caricature feel authentic and recognizable; specifics (boxing-matches, cock-fights, Bow bells) lend immediacy.
